title: Nasruddin Delivers a Letter
summary: A merchant asked Nasruddin to write a letter to a business partner in Damascus. Nasruddin agreed and scribbled two pages of bizarre, jagged lines....
full_text:
A merchant asked Nasruddin to write a letter to a business partner in Damascus. Nasruddin agreed and scribbled two pages of bizarre, jagged lines.

"Now, Mulla," said the merchant, "please give it to the courier."

"No," said Nasruddin, "if this letter is to reach Damascus, you must pay for my travel expenses so I can accompany the letter in person!"

"Why on earth must you go along?" asked the merchant.

"Because my handwriting is so uniquely profound that no human being in Damascus can read it unless I am standing right beside them to explain what it means!"
moral: When skill is lacking, inventive excuses disguise human limitation.
